Hi Sara — thanks for the details and the usage report. Below are three realistic upgrade paths and the associated levers. I've attached a compact package matrix that lays out feature sets and proration rules.

1) Standard Plus (minimal bump)
- What you get: 2x throughput headroom, longer short-term KV cache (30 min), same shared pool with burst enabled.
- When to pick: if you want smoother performance without full isolation.
- Pricing: ~ +15% on current spend; proration applied daily for mid-cycle upgrades.

2) Premium (recommended for predictable pilot)
- What you get: Dedicated capacity pool (option to reserve), priority routing, 90-day retention SLAs on logs/traces, built-in private VPC option for pilot.
- When to pick: pilot with 75 seats where latency and predictable throughput matter.
- Pricing: base +45% on current spend.

3) Private Dedicated (full isolation)
- What you get: customer-dedicated GPUs, VPC + HSM/KMS integrations, extended audit window, enterprise SLA.
- When to pick: regulated workloads or >100 seats.
- Pricing: custom — typically +80%+, includes deployment/setup fees.

Commitment discounts (guideline): 6-month commit = 10% off list; 12-month commit = 20% off list. We can also offer an onboarding/migration credit to soften the first quarter. Proration: upgrades are prorated by day; downgrades are applied at next renewal unless we agree on a partial credit.

Recommended next step: 30-minute call to align on the pilot success metrics (SLOs, seat ramp, data residency) — I can run numbers live and produce an apples-to-apples monthly estimate for 75 seats.

Cheers,
